criteria.criterion: Avoids a universal rule and frames a decision
criteria.evidence: It rejects both extremes: "Why you can't just leave it" and "Why you can't just delete it". It then frames the choice as "Remove it, but as a staged experiment with a way to detect failure".

criteria.criterion: Requires the workaround record fields (owner, scope, side effects, detection, exit)
criteria.evidence: Several fields are covered. History and reason: "Day 1: find the history". Side effects: "Every network node loses DHCP at the same moment". Detection: the drift check. Exit: "If drift never appears, delete the check too" and "a documented remediation". No owner is ever assigned, and the response never asks for a formal workaround record.

criteria.criterion: Proposes bounded testing of removal with detection and rollback
criteria.evidence: "Disable the cron on one node... Keep the drift check running and alert on it. Define rollback criteria up front... Rollback means re-enabling the cron." It then widens to the other nodes one at a time.

It notes the restart has its own side effects and that it "hides whatever the real fault is". It also warns that "the cron may stop covering it". It never says the workaround has become part of the system, or that other things may now depend on it.

criteria.criterion: Applies the 'risk introduced vs risk removed' test
criteria.evidence: There is an informal cost comparison: "A staged rollout over a few days costs almost nothing, while a fleet-wide DHCP failure costs far more." It also weighs the risk of the restart against the risk of removing it. It never states the principle that a change is safe only while the risk it introduces is less than the risk it removes.

critical_errors.error: recommends removing it across all nodes immediately without detection or rollback
critical_errors.evidence: It recommends a one-node canary with drift detection and rollback criteria. It also says to "push back on the method" if removal everywhere tonight is demanded.

critical_errors.error: recommends keeping it indefinitely without owner or review
critical_errors.evidence: It recommends removing the cron in stages, or replacing it with a restart that runs only when drift is detected. It does not recommend keeping the cron indefinitely.

summary: A strong, practical answer. It rejects both extremes and proposes a canary with detection and rollback that widens one node at a time. It also investigates the root cause and replaces the nightly ritual with a restart that runs only when drift is detected. It falls short in three areas. It never assigns an owner or asks for an explicit workaround record. It only touches on accidental architecture. Its risk comparison is informal rather than the stated 'risk introduced < risk removed' test. It commits no critical errors and has no faithfulness issues.
